```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Ramakrishnan and Mager (2019) built pharmacodynamic systems models that link
bortezomib exposure in cell culture to myeloma cell death through the dynamics
of ten intracellular signaling proteins. One model was built per cell line, on
data from a single 20 nM bortezomib exposure: the "less sensitive" U266 and
RPMI8226 cells and the "more sensitive" MM.1S and NCI-H929 cells. The four
models share a backbone (bortezomib stimulates pJNK, pNFkB and pAKT; the
downstream proteins follow indirect-response turnover equations; growth and
death of the cells are driven multiplicatively by the proteins) and differ in
transit compartments, power coefficients and a few protein-protein links. The
paper contributes four model files:

```{r models}
cell_lines <- c("U266", "RPMI8226", "MM.1S", "NCI-H929")
model_names <- c(
  "U266" = "Ramakrishnan_2019_bortezomib_u266",
  "RPMI8226" = "Ramakrishnan_2019_bortezomib_rpmi8226",
  "MM.1S" = "Ramakrishnan_2019_bortezomib_mm1s",
  "NCI-H929" = "Ramakrishnan_2019_bortezomib_ncih929"
)
mods <- lapply(model_names, function(nm) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm)))
```

```{r model-table, echo = FALSE}
tibble::tibble(
  file = unname(model_names),
  line = cell_lines,
  structure = c(
    "Transit compartments: pJNK 1, pNFkB 2, pAKT 1, pBAD 2. pp53 present. Powers on pp53 -> p21, pBAD -> Bcl-2, caspase 8 -> caspase 9. Cell-equation proteins held at their 24 h values.",
    "Transit compartments: pJNK 0, pNFkB 1, pAKT 1, pBAD 3. pp53 present. Powers on pNFkB -| caspase 8, pJNK -> pp53, pJNK -| pBAD, caspase 8 -> caspase 9 and pp53 -> p21.",
    "Transit compartments: pJNK 2, pNFkB 2, pAKT 1, pBAD 0. No pp53; bortezomib stimulates p21 directly (power on concentration). No pAKT -| p21, no pNFkB -> Bcl-2. Cell-equation proteins held at their 24 h values.",
    "Transit compartments: pJNK 0, pNFkB 2, pAKT 1, pBAD 1. No pp53; bortezomib stimulates p21 directly. pAKT -| p21 and pNFkB -> Bcl-2 retained. Powers on pJNK -> caspase 8, pJNK -| pBAD, pBAD -> Bcl-2."
  )
) |>
  dplyr::rename("nlmixr2lib model" = file, "Cell line" = line, "Network (Figure 1)" = structure) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "The four model files contributed by Ramakrishnan 2019.")
```

* Citation: `r mods[[1]]$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12358>
* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6430155/>

Supplementary Data S1 prints the equations for U266 (Eqs. 1-19) and MM.1S
(Eqs. 20-34) and describes the RPMI8226 and NCI-H929 models by their
differences from those two. Supplementary Data S2 is the authors' ADAPT 5 code
for the RPMI8226 model, which settles that model's equations and supplies the
variance model and the separate growth equation of the untreated control.
Table 1 of the article gives every parameter estimate.

# Population

The models were fitted to in vitro time courses from Ramakrishnan and Mager
2018 (J Pharmacol Exp Ther 365:734-751). Each of the four human multiple
myeloma cell lines was exposed to 20 nM bortezomib or left untreated. Ten
signaling proteins (pNFkB, pAKT, pmTOR, Bcl-2, pJNK, pp53, p21, pBAD, caspase 8
and caspase 9) were measured by Western blot and expressed relative to the
untreated control at 0 h. Viable-cell numbers were followed for 96 h and
likewise normalised to the untreated control at 0 h. Protein data after 24 h
were left out of model development because the cells were essentially all
dead by 24-30 h. The data were analysed by naive pooling with maximum
likelihood in ADAPT 5, so the models carry no between-well variability.

U266 and RPMI8226 carry a mutated TP53 gene and showed pp53 activation;
MM.1S and NCI-H929 carry wild-type TP53, showed no pp53 change, and have no
pp53 node.

```{r population}
str(mods[["U266"]]$population)
```

# Source trace

Each `ini()` entry carries its source in an in-file comment. The table collects
them. Parameter names are the same across the four files; a dash means the
parameter is not part of that cell line's model.

```{r source-trace, echo = FALSE}
trace_param <- function(ui) {
  d <- ui$iniDf
  d <- d[!is.na(d$ntheta), c("name", "est", "fix")]
  val <- ifelse(grepl("^l", d$name), exp(d$est), d$est)
  stats::setNames(
    ifelse(d$fix, paste0(signif(val, 4), " (fixed)"), as.character(signif(val, 4))),
    d$name
  )
}
vals <- lapply(mods, trace_param)
all_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(vals, names)))
trace_tab <- data.frame(parameter = all_names)
for (cl in cell_lines) {
  v <- vals[[cl]][all_names]
  trace_tab[[cl]] <- ifelse(is.na(v), "-", v)
}
trace_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Parameter (back-transformed)" = parameter) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 1 of Ramakrishnan 2019, by cell line (rate constants in 1/h, slopes in 1/nM).")
```

| Equation / parameter | Source location |
|----------------------|-----------------|
| Protein initial conditions = 1, synthesis rate = loss rate | Data S1 Eq. 1 |
| Variance model `Var = (sigma1 + sigma2 * Y)^2`, separate sigma for proteins and cells | Data S1 Eq. 2; Data S2 subroutine VARMOD |
| U266 protein equations | Data S1 Eqs. 3-18 |
| MM.1S protein equations | Data S1 Eqs. 20-33 |
| RPMI8226 protein equations | Data S2 subroutine DIFFEQ, XP(1)-XP(16) |
| NCI-H929 protein equations | Data S1 'NCI-H929' paragraph applied to MM.1S Eqs. 20-33; Figure 1d |
| Cell growth and death | Main text Eq. 1; Data S1 Eqs. 19 and 34; Data S2 XP(18) |
| Untreated control growth `d(control)/dt = kg * control` | Data S2 XP(17) |
| 24 h hold of the cell-equation proteins (U266, MM.1S) | Data S1, paragraphs after Eqs. 19 and 34 |
| Bortezomib half-life in medium, 144 h | Main text Methods; Data S2 `KDEG = 0.0048135208` |
| `lktr_*`, `lkdeg_*`, `slope_*`, `gamma_*`, `lkgrow`, `lkdeath` | Table 1, per cell line |
| `propSd_*` (proteins), `propSd_mm_cells*` (cells) | Table 1 'sigma2 Protein' and 'sigma2 MMcell' |

# Simulation

Every simulation below is a typical-value solve of the deterministic model.
Treatment is a 20 nM dose into the `media` compartment at time 0; the
untreated arm has no dose.

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 96, by = 0.5), 2, 6, 12, 24)))
proteins <- c("pnfkb", "pakt", "pmtor", "bcl2", "pjnk", "pp53", "p21", "pbad", "cas8", "cas9")
protein_labels <- c(
  pnfkb = "pNFkB", pakt = "pAKT", pmtor = "pmTOR", bcl2 = "Bcl-2", pjnk = "pJNK",
  pp53 = "pp53", p21 = "p21", pbad = "pBAD", cas8 = "Cas 8", cas9 = "Cas 9"
)

solve_line <- function(ui, dose_nM, times) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(times, cmt = "mm_cells")
  if (dose_nM > 0) ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = dose_nM, cmt = "media", time = 0)
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
}

sims <- bind_rows(lapply(cell_lines, function(cl) {
  treated <- solve_line(mods[[cl]], 20, obs_times)
  untreated <- solve_line(mods[[cl]], 0, obs_times)
  bind_rows(
    mutate(treated, cell_line = cl, arm = "Bortezomib 20 nM"),
    mutate(untreated, cell_line = cl, arm = "Untreated")
  )
}))
sims$cell_line <- factor(sims$cell_line, levels = cell_lines)
```

## Untreated steady state

Without bortezomib every protein synthesis rate equals its loss rate, so all
proteins stay at their initial value of 1, and the untreated control grows as
`exp(kg * t)`. Both sides of each comparison use the same parameters, so the
differences are pure numerical error and a tight bound is correct.

```{r steady-state}
untreated <- filter(sims, arm == "Untreated")
max_protein_drift <- untreated |>
  select(any_of(proteins)) |>
  as.matrix() |>
  (\(m) max(abs(m - 1), na.rm = TRUE))()
kg <- sapply(cell_lines, function(cl) exp(mods[[cl]]$theta[["lkgrow"]]))
control_err <- untreated |>
  mutate(expected = exp(kg[as.character(cell_line)] * time)) |>
  summarise(max_rel = max(abs(mm_cells_control / expected - 1))) |>
  pull(max_rel)
c(max_protein_drift = max_protein_drift, max_control_rel_err = control_err)
stopifnot(max_protein_drift < 1e-8, control_err < 1e-5)
```

The treated-cell equation is not the untreated control: with no drug its
right-hand side reduces to `(kg - kd) * cells`, which for RPMI8226
(`kd > kg`) would make untreated cells decline. The paper fitted the untreated
cells with the separate first-order growth equation of its code, and the
models carry it as `mm_cells_control`. Use `mm_cells_control` for an untreated
arm and `mm_cells` for a treated arm.

## Figures 2 and 3: protein heatmaps

The heatmaps replicate the "Model fits" panels of Figures 2a, 2c, 3a and 3c:
log10 relative expression at the experimental sampling times. MM.1S and
NCI-H929 have no pp53 node.

```{r heatmap, fig.height = 7}
heat <- sims |>
  filter(arm == "Bortezomib 20 nM", time %in% c(0, 2, 6, 12, 24)) |>
  select(cell_line, time, any_of(proteins)) |>
  pivot_longer(any_of(proteins), names_to = "protein", values_to = "rel") |>
  filter(!is.na(rel)) |>
  mutate(
    protein = factor(protein_labels[protein], levels = rev(protein_labels)),
    log_rel = log10(rel)
  )
ggplot(heat, aes(factor(time), protein, fill = log_rel)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#00008F", "#0080FF", "#80FFFF", "#FFFF00", "#FF8000", "#800000"),
    name = "log10 relative\nexpression"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~cell_line, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Figures 2 and 3: cell proliferation

Replicates Figures 2b, 2d, 3b and 3d: viable cells relative to the untreated
control at 0 h, untreated and under 20 nM bortezomib.

```{r cells}
ggplot(sims, aes(time, ifelse(arm == "Untreated", mm_cells_control, mm_cells), colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Bortezomib 20 nM" = "blue", "Untreated" = "black")) +
  facet_wrap(~cell_line, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cell viability (relative to untreated control at 0 h)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r cells-check}
cell_summary <- sims |>
  filter(time %in% c(24, 96)) |>
  transmute(
    cell_line, time,
    value = ifelse(arm == "Untreated", mm_cells_control, mm_cells),
    arm
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(arm, time), values_from = value)
knitr::kable(cell_summary, digits = 3)
viab24 <- setNames(cell_summary[["Bortezomib 20 nM_24"]], as.character(cell_summary$cell_line))
control96 <- setNames(cell_summary[["Untreated_96"]], as.character(cell_summary$cell_line))
stopifnot(
  # Figures 2b, 2d, 3b, 3d: the untreated curves end near 6, 5, 6 and 9.
  abs(control96[["U266"]] / 6.1 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(control96[["RPMI8226"]] / 5.0 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(control96[["MM.1S"]] / 6.2 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(control96[["NCI-H929"]] / 9.0 - 1) < 0.1,
  # Sensitivity order of the paper: U266 > RPMI8226 > NCI-H929 > MM.1S
  # surviving at 24 h (Figure 5b).
  identical(names(sort(viab24, decreasing = TRUE)), c("U266", "RPMI8226", "NCI-H929", "MM.1S"))
)
```

The untreated controls end at the values of the published curves. The treated
cells of the two "more sensitive" lines are almost all dead by 12 h, and those
of the "less sensitive" lines fall more slowly, as in the figures.

# Figure 5: protein AUEC and drug sensitivity

The paper correlated the area under each model-fitted protein expression
curve from 0 to 24 h (AUEC) with cell viability at 24 h across the four
lines. The AUEC that reproduces Figure 5b is the linear-trapezoidal area of
relative expression minus its baseline of 1, taken over the experimental
sampling times (0, 2, 6, 12 and 24 h). It is computed with PKNCA here: the
`auclast` of relative expression over 0-24 h minus the baseline area of 24.

```{r pknca}
auec_input <- sims |>
  filter(arm == "Bortezomib 20 nM", time %in% c(0, 2, 6, 12, 24)) |>
  select(cell_line, time, any_of(proteins)) |>
  pivot_longer(any_of(proteins), names_to = "protein", values_to = "rel") |>
  filter(!is.na(rel)) |>
  mutate(id = 1L, cell_line = as.character(cell_line))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(auec_input, rel ~ time | cell_line + protein + id)
nca_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE),
  options = list(auc.method = "linear")
)
nca_res <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(nca_data))
auec <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  transmute(cell_line, protein, auec = PPORRES - 24)
```

Figure 5b plots the AUEC of pNFkB, pAKT and caspase 8 on a log axis. The
values below were digitised by the maintainers from marker centroids against
the axis ticks (about 3% per pixel).

```{r fig5b}
fig5b <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cell_line, ~protein, ~published,
  "U266", "pnfkb", 32.0,
  "U266", "pakt", 64.0,
  "U266", "cas8", 91.5,
  "RPMI8226", "pnfkb", 4.52,
  "RPMI8226", "pakt", 56.2,
  "RPMI8226", "cas8", 10.75,
  "MM.1S", "pnfkb", 334,
  "MM.1S", "pakt", 125.3,
  "MM.1S", "cas8", 1380,
  "NCI-H929", "pnfkb", 333.6,
  "NCI-H929", "pakt", 102.9,
  "NCI-H929", "cas8", 253
)
fig5b_cmp <- fig5b |>
  left_join(auec, by = c("cell_line", "protein")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auec / published - 1))
fig5b_cmp |>
  mutate(protein = protein_labels[protein]) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cell line" = cell_line, "Protein" = protein,
    "Figure 5b AUEC" = published, "Simulated AUEC" = auec, "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  nrow(fig5b_cmp) == 12, !anyNA(fig5b_cmp$auec),
  max(abs(fig5b_cmp$pct_diff)) < 8
)
```

All twelve digitised AUECs are reproduced within the digitisation error. They
come from four separately fitted models, so the agreement checks every
cell-line file, including the NCI-H929 model, whose equations are not printed
and were assembled from the text.

Figure 5a gives the Spearman rank correlation between viability at 24 h and
the AUEC of each protein. Bcl-2 and pBAD are inhibited, so their AUEC is
negative; the published negative coefficients for them ("increasing
inhibition of Bcl-2 and pBAD", Discussion) correspond to correlating viability
with the size of the inhibition, so their AUEC is taken as a magnitude.
The simulated viabilities rank the cell lines in the same order as the
observed viabilities of Figure 5b (U266 0.22, RPMI8226 0.11, NCI-H929 0.02,
MM.1S 0.004), so the rank correlation is fully determined by the model.

```{r fig5a}
fig5a <- c(pnfkb = -0.8, pakt = -0.8, pmtor = -0.4, bcl2 = -0.6, pjnk = 0.2, pbad = -0.6, cas8 = -0.8, cas9 = -0.4)
rho <- sapply(names(fig5a), function(p) {
  a <- auec |>
    filter(protein == p) |>
    mutate(auec = if (p %in% c("bcl2", "pbad")) abs(auec) else auec)
  stopifnot(nrow(a) == 4)
  stats::cor(viab24[a$cell_line], a$auec, method = "spearman")
})
data.frame(protein = protein_labels[names(fig5a)], published = fig5a, simulated = rho) |>
  dplyr::rename("Protein" = protein, "Figure 5a rho" = published, "Simulated rho" = simulated) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(abs(rho - fig5a) < 1e-8))
```

All eight published coefficients are reproduced exactly. With four cell lines
a Spearman coefficient moves in steps of 0.2, so this checks the rank order of
the simulated AUECs; the pNFkB AUECs of MM.1S and NCI-H929 differ by under 1%,
and only the sampling-time trapezoid reproduces the published -0.8 for pNFkB.

# Reproduction gate: the authors' RPMI8226 code

Supplementary Data S2 is the ADAPT 5 Fortran of the RPMI8226 model. Below it
is transcribed line by line, separately from the model file and with the
ADAPT state numbering, and solved with the Table 1 values. Both sides solve
the same deterministic ODE with the same parameters, so the difference is
numerical error only and a tight bound is correct.

```{r adapt-code}
adapt_rpmi <- rxode2::rxode2({
  kspjnk <- kdpjnk
  kspnfkb <- kdpnfkb
  kscas8 <- kdcas8
  kspakt <- kdpakt
  kspmtor <- kdpmtor
  kspp53 <- kdpp53
  kspbad <- kdpbad
  ksbcl2 <- kdbcl2
  kscas9 <- kdcas9
  ksp21 <- kdp21
  KDEG <- 0.0048135208
  d/dt(X1) <- -KDEG * X1
  d/dt(X2) <- kspjnk * (1 + (smpjnk * X1)) - kdpjnk * X2
  d/dt(X3) <- (kscas8 / (X5^GC8)) * (X2) - kdcas8 * X3
  d/dt(X4) <- kspnfkb * (1 + (smpnfkb * X1^G)) - kdpnfkb * X4
  d/dt(X5) <- kdpnfkb * (X4 - X5)
  d/dt(X6) <- kspakt * (1 + smpakt * X1) - kdpakt * X6
  d/dt(X7) <- kdpakt * (X6 - X7)
  d/dt(X8) <- kspmtor * (X7) - kdpmtor * X8
  d/dt(X9) <- (kspp53 / (X7)) * (X2^G53) - kdpp53 * X9
  d/dt(X10) <- kspbad - kdpbad * (X2^GB2) * X10
  d/dt(X11) <- kdpbad * (X10 - X11)
  d/dt(X12) <- kdpbad * (X11 - X12)
  d/dt(X13) <- kdpbad * (X12 - X13)
  d/dt(X14) <- (ksbcl2 / X9) * (X13) * (X5) - kdbcl2 * X14
  d/dt(X15) <- kscas9 * (1 / X14) * (1 / X5) * (X3^GC9) - kdcas9 * X15
  d/dt(X16) <- (ksp21 / (X7)) * (X9^G21) - kdp21 * X16
  d/dt(X17) <- kg * X17
  d/dt(X18) <- (kg / (X16)) * (X8) * X7 * X18 - kd * X3 * (X15) * X18
})
# Table 1, RPMI8226, in the ADAPT symbol names. G (power of the bortezomib
# term for pNFkB) is not among the estimates and is 1.
p_adapt <- c(
  kdpjnk = 0.07269, smpjnk = 0.2965, G = 1, kdcas8 = 0.1656, kdpnfkb = 0.07685,
  smpnfkb = 0.04046, GC8 = 5.640, kdpakt = 0.04528, smpakt = 1.011,
  kdpmtor = 0.0007853, kdpp53 = 0.04395, G53 = 1.746, kdpbad = 0.2257,
  kdbcl2 = 0.008890, GB2 = 0.3705, kdcas9 = 0.008027, GC9 = 5, kdp21 = 0.01834,
  G21 = 5, kg = 0.01680, kd = 0.05166
)
inits <- c(X1 = 20, stats::setNames(rep(1, 17), paste0("X", 2:18)))
ref <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(adapt_rpmi, p_adapt, rxode2::et(obs_times), inits = inits))
pkg <- filter(sims, cell_line == "RPMI8226", arm == "Bortezomib 20 nM")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(ref$time, pkg$time)))
map <- c(
  X2 = "pjnk", X3 = "cas8", X5 = "pnfkb", X7 = "pakt", X8 = "pmtor", X9 = "pp53",
  X13 = "pbad", X14 = "bcl2", X15 = "cas9", X16 = "p21", X18 = "mm_cells"
)
rel_err <- sapply(names(map), function(x) max(abs(pkg[[map[[x]]]] / ref[[x]] - 1)))
signif(rel_err, 2)
stopifnot(all(rel_err < 1e-4))
```

The packaged RPMI8226 model reproduces the authors' code to solver
precision for all ten proteins and the treated cells.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error.** Data S1 Eq. 2 defines the variance as
  `(sigma1 + sigma2 * Y)^2`, and Table 1 reports only `sigma2` (one value for
  all proteins and one for the cells) for each cell line. The intercept
  `sigma1` is not reported, so the models carry a purely proportional error
  with SD `sigma2`. rxode2 cannot tie one residual parameter to several
  endpoints, so each protein endpoint carries its own copy of the shared
  protein value (and each cell endpoint of the shared cell value); a refit
  that wants the paper's structure should constrain them to be equal.
* **RPMI8226 pNFkB stimulation.** The authors' code writes the bortezomib term
  for pNFkB as `smpnfkb * X(1)**G`. `G` is not among the Table 1 estimates,
  the text describes every bortezomib stimulation as linear, and Data S1 lists
  the RPMI8226 power coefficients without it, so the term is linear (`G = 1`).
  The code's unused parameter `GG` is dropped. The Figure 2c model-fit pNFkB
  profile and the Figure 5 pNFkB AUEC (4.5) are reproduced with `G = 1`.
* **NCI-H929 equations.** Data S1 describes the NCI-H929 model as the MM.1S
  model with: no pJNK transit compartment; one pBAD transit compartment; power
  coefficients on pJNK stimulation of caspase 8, pJNK-stimulated loss of pBAD
  and pBAD stimulation of Bcl-2; no power on bortezomib in the p21 equation
  (Table 1 has no `gamma p21` for NCI-H929); and the retained pAKT inhibition
  of p21 and pNFkB stimulation of Bcl-2. The two retained links are written in
  the form they take in the U266 equations (division by pAKT, multiplication
  by pNFkB). The resulting model reproduces Figure 5 (above).
* **NCI-H929 `k dpBAD`.** Table 1 lists the NCI-H929 pBAD rate as
  'k dpBAD' with the description 'pBAD transit rate constant'; with one
  transit compartment it is the shared rate of the transit chain
  (`lktr_pbad`). Likewise the NCI-H929 'k tpJNK' acts as the pJNK turnover
  rate (`lkdeg_pjnk`) because that line has no pJNK transit compartment.
* **24 h hold (U266, MM.1S).** For these two lines the final cell-dynamics
  parameters were estimated with pAKT, pmTOR, p21, caspase 8 and caspase 9
  fixed at their 24 h values in the cell equation. The models reproduce this
  with five `_held` states that follow the proteins until 24 h and stay
  constant afterwards; the protein states themselves keep evolving. The hold
  is tied to the model's time 0, so treatment should start at time 0.
* **Untreated control.** The untreated cells follow the separate
  `d(control)/dt = kg * control` equation of the authors' code (Data S2,
  XP(17)), stated there for RPMI8226 and assumed for the other three lines
  (Data S2: "the code files ... for U266, MM.1S and NCI-H929 cells were
  implemented similarly"). The untreated curves of Figures 2 and 3 are
  reproduced.
* **Fixed values.** Table 1 marks five power coefficients with an asterisk and
  no %CV (U266 `gamma Bcl-2` = 5 and `gamma p21` = 2.5, RPMI8226 `gamma p21`
  and `gamma Cas9` = 5, MM.1S `gamma Bcl-2` = 5 and `gamma p21` = 1.2); the
  footnote does not define the asterisk, and they are encoded as fixed.
* **Bortezomib in the medium.** The paper takes the 144 h half-life in medium
  from Chudasama 2015; it is fixed. Bortezomib concentration is the dose in nM
  given to `media`; there is no volume.
* **Scope.** Each model was fitted to a single 20 nM exposure, so responses to
  other concentrations are extrapolations (the paper notes the models cannot
  account for dose-dependent nonlinearities).
* A dated check on 2026-11-25 found no erratum or correction for the article
  in Europe PMC.
